column1: # DESIGN NOTE (this is the load-bearing decision):
#   These patterns are a ONE-TIME CANDIDATE GENERATOR, not the source of truth.
#   Route order is /gene -> /product -> manual coords. Every hit is then verified
#   by hand and FROZEN as (coords + aa_sha256) into the seed table. Afterwards
#   re-extraction is a REGRESSION TEST against the frozen SHA, so a future RefSeq
#   re-annotation that renames the product breaks the test loudly instead of
#   silently dropping the gene. Patterns may therefore be generous: recall here,
# aa_min/aa_max: sanity window only (S4 step 3: 40-260 aa for exclusion factors);
#   a hit outside the window is FLAGGED for review, never auto-dropped.

column1: # WHY name_regex AND phenotype_regex ARE SEPARATE COLUMNS
# Three false positives, all the same failure mode: a PHENOTYPE phrase in
#   "surface exclusion"    -> F/R100 traS and traT carry the IDENTICAL product
#                             string, so the traT pattern matched the traS CDS
#   "aggregation substance" -> matched pAM373 EP0041 (PrgB/Asc10 class), which
#                             broke the negative arm; PrgA is surface exclusion,
#                             the aggregation substance is a different protein
#                             exclusion lipoprotein at 35.7 kb) and filed it as
#                             IncC eexC, producing a nonsense 128 kb adjacency
# name_regex assigns identity and contains gene-NAME tokens ONLY.
# phenotype_regex never assigns identity; it only FLAGS a CDS for human review.
# A phenotype phrase says what a protein does, not which gene it is.
